messages:
carmen: Quick follow-up from the loading RFC — we hit a production flake where a lazy-activated shard got evicted during activation and ended up with a KV-cache mismatch. I want to discuss activation ordering guarantees and a small API tweak to make warmup safe under evictions.

raj: ouch, can you paste the minimal repro or traces? was it a double-free or stale mapping?

carmen: attaching rough trace inlined: `activate_shard(id=shard-42) -> mmap; eviction(seq=87) triggered -> unmap; activate callback writes KV offsets -> segfault` ; looks like activation assumed pin permanence.

emily: this is why we need an explicit Acquire/Release semantic rather than implicit pin-on-activate. Activation should be idempotent and fail fast if the memory view changed mid-op.

dave: agreed on idempotence. two options: 1) coarse-grained global activation lock (simple but kills throughput), 2) per-shard activation token + optimistic install with CAS validation.

raj: +1 for token/CAS. sketch: runtime exposes `ActivateShard(shard_id, activation_token)` where activation_token carries expected metadata hash (sha256 of header+pages). Activate is atomic: it validates current eviction_epoch and installs pointer if match, otherwise returns RETRY.

carmen: nice. what about compatibility with manifestless bundles and safetensors deltas? we sometimes apply patch overlays at activation time (delta patches for 8-bit quant).

emily: token should include a dependency graph digest. i.e. activation_token = {manifest_hash, delta_ids[], dependency_epoch}. runtime checks all dependency epochs. if any dependency changed, activate fails and caller must re-run prepare/patch.

raj: implementation detail: make the activation API asynchronous-friendly: return a small ActivationHandle that can be awaited. ActivationHandle.state in {PENDING, INSTALLED, ABORTED}. callers awaiting the handle get deterministic result.

dave: also add a light-weight validation step post-install where we verify a few sentinel bytes in the mapped memory match expected pattern (cheap checksum). avoids silent corruption when mapping races with zeroing.

carmen: how about eviction interplay? we want evictions to be able to preempt pending activations (to free memory quickly), but not leave partial installs.

raj: eviction should increment a shard_epoch counter. Activate compares the epoch at start and before final install; if epoch changed, it aborts. That plus CAS install gives atomicity.

emily: two perf tradeoffs: (A) keeping epoch checks frequent adds a few memory loads per activation, (B) holding a short-lived lock during install adds latency tails. I prefer epoch+CAS since epoch is just an integer and CAS is common on hot paths.

dave: another angle — provide a thin runtime guarantee: Activation is linearizable with respect to eviction. Either activation wins (shard becomes pinned) or eviction wins (shard not installed). No intermediate states visible. That contract keeps higher layers simpler.

carmen: do we want to expose these internals in the weightsource API? i.e. higher-level code calls `prepare_patch`, `activate`, `release`. or keep as `load()` and runtime hides phases?

raj: expose the phases. ops we need: `PrepareShard(shard_id, source, patches[]) -> prepare_token`, `ActivateShard(shard_id, prepare_token) -> activation_handle`, `PinShard(shard_id)`, `ReleaseShard(shard_id)`. callers that understand lifecycle can do optimistic background prepares.

emily: exposing phases gives us richer batching opportunities (prepare many shards in background). but API must be backwards-compatible with existing single-call `LoadShard` — we can add defaults that call the 3-phase flow under the hood.

carmen: sounds good. let's draft minimal proto signatures.

raj: proto sketch: ```proto
rpc PrepareShard(PrepareRequest) returns (PrepareResponse);
message PrepareRequest { string shard_id = 1; bytes source_ref = 2; repeated string patch_ids = 3; }
message PrepareResponse { string prepare_token = 1; uint64 expected_epoch = 2; bytes digest = 3; }

rpc ActivateShard(ActivateRequest) returns (ActivationResponse);
message ActivateRequest { string shard_id = 1; string prepare_token = 2; bytes expected_digest = 3; }
message ActivationResponse { string activation_handle = 1; enum Status { PENDING=0; INSTALLED=1; ABORTED=2; RETRY=3; } Status status = 2; }
```

dave: good. also add a light `ProbeShard(shard_id)` to query epoch/digest without forcing activation (useful for health checks).

emily: ops: we must update indexers to emit `manifest_hash` + `delta_chain` in the safetensors header when possible. falling back to sidecar manifest if not available. this improves token generation.

carmen: what about smaller safety-net: if prepare_token is missing (old bundles), runtime falls back to conservative single-call load that temporarily pins during install. compatibility mode flagged in PrepareResponse.

raj: also we should add a monitoring metric: activation_retries_per_min and activation_abort_rate; SLOs around activation success within X ms.

dave: rollout plan: implement epoch+CAS in runtime -> add ActivateShard proto -> backfill indexers to set manifest_hash -> opt-in flag `enable_atomic_activation` on dedicated clusters -> canary.

carmen: timeline proposal: prototype in runtime 2 weeks, prototype client API behind flag 1 week, indexer follow-up 2 weeks, canary next sprint.

deploybot: Canary for feature/atomic-activation deployed to eng-dedicated-canary at 2026-03-19T18:42:30Z :rocket:

emily: small open Q: should activation_token include an expected memory layout fingerprint (page-size alignment + hot-run offsets)? that helps detect subtle patch-application bugs.

raj: I'd keep fingerprinting minimal (header+digest). complicated memory-layout fingerprints increase fragility between runtimes and platforms. we can add optional debug-only fingerprints.

carmen: ok. let's summarize action items: 1) raj/dave: draft runtime patch (epoch+CAS + ActivationHandle). 2) emily: update indexer to emit manifest_hash and optional delta list. 3) carmen: draft proto and compatibility notes for SDKs. 4) ops: add metrics and flag for canary. I'll create an RFC follow-up doc with these next steps.

raj: lgtm. I'll open a PR for the runtime sketch today.

emily: thanks — ping me on the PR, I'll wire the indexer changes.

carmen: thanks everyone. moving this to docs/eng-ml/atomic-activation-rfc-draft next. :white_check_mark:
